name: Viking Raid on Lindisfarne
summary: On 8 June 793, Norse raiders attacked the monastery of Lindisfarne (Holy Island) off the Northumbrian coast, killing monks, plundering the treasury, and burning buildings. The attack shocked the Christian world: Alcuin of York wrote that such wickedness had never been seen in Britain before. The Lindisfarne raid is conventionally taken as the beginning of the Viking Age, two and a half centuries of Scandinavian raids, settlement, and state-building across Europe.
outcomes: Scholars and clerics killed or enslaved
Christendom shocked by pagan assault on holy site

_quarry.structural_significance: The symbolic opening of the Viking Age; the shock it produced throughout Christendom marked the arrival of a new force that would reshape the political map of Europe.

sources_used: Haywood, The Penguin Historical Atlas of the Vikings
Jones, A History of the Vikings
